title: How Adam Robinson scaled RB2B to $5M ARR in 13 months with five people
summary: Adam tells the years-long backstory behind RB2B: a stuck email app, a feature customers loved, and a pivot found through LinkedIn posts. He covers validating demand with 300 discovery calls, a free Slack integration, pricing mistakes, founder-brand distribution, radical transparency, and keeping the team tiny.

principles.text: Overnight success is years of head-banging; the unlock then arrives all at once.
principles.quote: it was the two years before it and banging my head against the wall that actually like allowed for that unlock. But the unlock happened all at once.

principles.text: Test a new audience with posts before building, then confirm with discovery calls.
principles.quote: I know exactly how to write a post for a B2B revenue leader that will crush.

principles.text: In discovery, ask about the current workflow and what people complain about, not about your idea.
principles.quote: like how are you using website identity right now? Like how is that information getting to your reps, right? Like what are some things that they complain about?

principles.text: Give away the magic moment for free and charge for the rest; the free Slack integration drove virality.
principles.quote: if you really want this to go viral, I think we need to give the Slack integration for free. because that's the magic moment

principles.text: In a distrusted category, build trust by sharing everything publicly, including money numbers.
principles.quote: if I'm inherently in an inherently untrustworthy product category, how do I build the maximum amount of trust? It's like, well, I share literally everything about what I'm doing, right?

principles.text: Keep the team small on purpose; set a headcount rule so everyone wears many hats and focus is forced.
principles.quote: We literally just declared it. We're like, we're not going to hire anyone until we're above 10.
